subject: API key exposure discovery — request for IR plan and evidence
messages:
From: Jane Thompson <jane.thompson@finbridge.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finbridge.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Possible exposure of API keys — seeking confirmation and next steps

Hi Rafael,

We discovered suspicious activity in our integration logs yesterday evening that looks like several of our service keys were used from IPs we do not recognize. We rotated our keys immediately but wanted to confirm whether any of our requests hit Redwood endpoints with an abnormal pattern and whether your team can provide relevant access logs and your incident response plan.

Two urgent asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether FinBridge keys were used against your hosted API between Nov 20–21?
- We need an IR contact and a short summary of Redwood's playbook (what evidence you will share, expected timelines).

I can pull additional artifacts on our side if helpful. Please let me know the best person to coordinate with.

Thanks,
Jane Thompson
Head of Platform Security
FinBridge

--
Attachment: none (we have exported our suspicious request dump and can share if requested)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Thompson <jane.thompson@finbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of API keys — seeking confirmation and next steps

Hi Jane — thanks for the heads up and sorry to hear about the suspicious activity. I’ve looped in Marissa (customer security lead) and Diego (infra/on-call) to help triage.

Short answers up front:
- We will check FinBridge key usage across hosted endpoints for Nov 20–21 and provide a sanitized access log extract.
- Our IR point is marissa_cole@redwood.ai; we typically provide a short evidence bundle (access logs, request IDs, region/time slices), a chronology of observed activity, and recommended mitigation steps within 24–48 hours for incidents of this scope.

Next steps we’ll take today:
1) Diego will search request logs and KV cache hits for the token identifiers and return matching request IDs and originating IPs.
2) Marissa will assemble the IR evidence packet and share via secure Drive link and escalate to our SOC if we see indicators of compromise.
3) Rafael (me) will keep you updated on timeline; expect first packet within 12 hours.

Can you confirm whether FinBridge rotated keys already and whether you’ve shared any of the suspicious request payloads? If you can attach a short sample, it will speed matching.

Rafael
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: none

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Jane Thompson <jane.thompson@finbridge.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of API keys — search results and logs

Hi all — quick update from infra. I searched our request logs and found 17 distinct request IDs that used tokens tied to FinBridge customer IDs between 2026-11-20T03:10:00Z and 2026-11-21T22:43:12Z. Origin IPs include three addresses outside FinBridge's normal CIDR ranges. I exported a sanitized CSV of the matching rows (access_logs_20261121.csv) and a short text file listing temporary keys that appear in the requests (temporary_keys_listing.txt).

Observations:
- No obvious mass data exfiltration patterns; most requests were small inference calls, but there are a few higher-than-usual token counts.
- The IPs are not associated with any of our known partners or cloud providers in the standard allowlist.
- KV cache access patterns look normal; we did not see cache key tampering.

What I will include in the evidence bundle: logs CSV (sanitized IPs replaced with ASN-tags for privacy), request ID list, timeline, and SHA256 checksums for the artifacts. I recommend FinBridge rotate any keys that may have been leaked and create replacements while we complete a deeper review.

Diego
SRE — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: access_logs_20261121.csv, temporary_keys_listing.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Thompson <jane.thompson@finbridge.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Possible exposure of API keys — evidence bundle and IR plan

Hi Jane — attaching the initial evidence bundle via Drive link and summarizing our IR plan below. We attached artifacts to the Drive folder (see link) and included checksums in the manifest.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-IR-Evidence (access granted to finbridge@finbridge.com)
Artifacts included: access_logs_20261121.csv, temporary_keys_listing.txt, short-chronology.txt, ir_playbook_v2.pdf

IR plan (high level):
- T0–T12 hours: validate matches, share sanitized logs and request IDs (done).
- T12–T48 hours: deeper forensic review (edge logs, container-level telemetry), confirm scope of requests, and identify any suspicious artifacts. We will involve our SOC team if we see lateral activity.
- T48–T120 hours: postmortem and remediation report (includes timeline, root cause hypothesis, control gaps, and recommended hardening).

Action items for FinBridge:
- Confirm key rotation (status + timestamp).
- Share any suspicious payloads or request IDs from your side to speed cross-matching.
- Confirm the FinBridge contact for evidence sharing (we granted drive access to finbridge@finbridge.com).

We will continue to coordinate closely. If you want real-time sync, I can set up a 30-minute bridge with our SOC and infra tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Security Lead
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: ir_playbook_v2.pdf, access_logs_20261121.csv, temporary_keys_listing.txt
